study type: Narrative Review/Commentary (referencing a meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials)
outcome: Neonatal complications (birth trauma, tube feeding, hypotonia)
cohort: The findings discussed are from a meta-analysis primarily focusing on singleton pregnancies, while future proposed trials would involve nulliparous, singleton, term, vertex pregnancies.
finding: A recent meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials indicated that planned cesarean delivery was associated with both benefits and risks for mothers and neonates when compared to planned vaginal delivery, influencing maternal and perinatal outcomes differently.
mod_finding: Planned cesarean delivery was associated with significantly decreased rates of low umbilical artery pH, neonatal complications (birth trauma, tube feeding, hypotonia), and perinatal death for infants, while reducing maternal chorioamnionitis but increasing wound infection and urinary incontinence, compared to planned vaginal delivery.
